=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: "Fail closed if identity cannot be established." — explicitly stated in the linked issue recommendation; the issue also explicitly requires the same fail-closed posture for the conflict-preparation state read ("Apply the same author restriction to conflict-preparation state reads").
  Expected change site: scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh, integration state read block (around the `else` arm at lines 513-520 where `_conflict_state_login` fails the regex check).
  Evidence of absence: The PR (original + last autofix) only adds a `::warning::review_conflict_prepare: pipeline identity unavailable; orchestrator state not read` log line, then falls through to the placeholder `INTEGRATION_MERGED_SUB_ISSUES_LIST="          (no merged sub-issues recorded in tracking-issue state — this typically means the integration branch is empty or state is not yet seeded)"` at lines 518-520, with `INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINTS_JSON` left at the initial `"{}"`. The script exits 0 and `IS_INTEGRATION_SYNC=true` is still exported at lines 530-534, so the downstream resolver (`review_conflict_resolve.sh`, gated on `IS_INTEGRATION_SYNC=true` at lines 1316, 1876, 2633) still receives `MERGED_SUB_ISSUES_LIST` (line 693) and `INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINTS_FILE` (line 525) as if the read had succeeded, with an attacker-poisonable merged-sub-issues section and an empty fingerprints map. By contrast, the poller-side fix in this same PR (`extract_latest_valid_orchestrator_state`) correctly sets `EXTRACTED_STATE_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE=true` and the main loop `continue`s; the equivalent fail-closed gate is missing here. An attacker who can both poison state and observe the placeholder warning has a path that the poller-side fix does not have.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- Requirement: "Fail closed if identity cannot be established."
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh`, integration state read block (lines 470-519)
  Evidence of absence: When identity lookup fails (lines 513-516), the script logs a warning but continues execution. The `if [[ "${_conflict_state_login}" =~ ... ]]` check fails, the else branch emits `::warning::review_conflict_prepare: pipeline identity unavailable; orchestrator state not read`, then the script unsets variables and proceeds. `INTEGRATION_MERGED_SUB_ISSUES_LIST` remains empty, triggering the fallback placeholder at lines 521-522 ("no merged sub-issues recorded"). The prepare step exits 0, and `review_autofix.yml` proceeds to its resolver step. The resolver then runs without trusted merged-sub-issue state or fingerprints — exactly the fail-open behavior the linked issue forbids. The poller path (`orchestrate_poll_process.sh`) correctly fails closed by returning 1 from the extractor and skipping processing, but the conflict-preparation path does not mirror this behavior.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- Requirement: "Before V1 or V2 extraction, accept state comments only from the verified pipeline identity; require every V2 chunk to meet that check and fail closed if identity cannot be established."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh, integration state read block (lines 470-519)
  Evidence of absence: When pipeline identity cannot be verified, the script only logs `::warning::review_conflict_prepare: pipeline identity unavailable; orchestrator state not read` and falls through to the placeholder path (`INTEGRATION_MERGED_SUB_ISSUES_LIST` set to the "no merged sub-issues recorded" string, `INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINTS_JSON` left as `{}`). The script exits successfully and `review_autofix.yml` proceeds to the resolver step with degraded context. The issue explicitly says "fail closed if identity cannot be established" — this path degrades instead. The added test `test_integration_resolver_state_context_requires_authenticated_author` with `identity_available=False` explicitly asserts the degradation behavior (`FINGERPRINTS={}`, `no merged sub-issues recorded`), confirming fail-closed was not implemented. The poller path in `orchestrate_poll_process.sh` correctly fails closed (skips the tick); the conflict-prepare path does not.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
